**Finding: deviation (high severity) — § 14.2 Deliverable licence**

The licence architecture in Section 13 already satisfies our preferred position:
- **§ 13.1** — Services licence names Customer, Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf.
- **§ 13.2** — paid-up software/Vendor Technology licence is perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free, with modification and contractor support rights.
- **§ 13.3** — transferable to an Affiliate or successor; revocation only for material uncured breach after notice and cure.

**§ 14.2 is the outlier** and sits at our walk-away line for Deliverables: "Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term." Deliverables are, by definition (§ 1.4), work product created specifically for us — so a revocable, term-limited licence with no Affiliate or contractor coverage is unacceptable and inconsistent with §§ 13.2–13.3 (and with § 14.3, which routes embedded Vendor Technology to the perpetual § 13.2 licence).

**Redline (validated, ok:true)** — replaces only the second sentence of § 14.2, preserving Vendor's ownership of Deliverables, with a perpetual, irrevocable, fully paid licence to Customer, its Affiliates and contractors, transferable and revocable only per § 13.3. The comment offers the fallback of transfer limited to an M&A successor.
